face: Begone from my sight, ser {player}, and take your sour face with you. The road is wide enough for us both, though I would not weep if we never met again.
Ride on, ser {player}. Your name will be sung in my hall as a cautionary tale, and I intend to sing it loudly.
Hell take the roads that brought you to me, ser {player}. Go, before my patience and my blade find some common ground.
Farewell, and mind the ditch on your way out. I would hate to hear the world swallowed you before my own vengeance could.
This parting pleases me more than any feast. Go, ser {player}, and carry your grievances to whatever tavern will still have you.
You leave with your purse and your pride both lighter, ser {player}. Remember that the debt between us is not yet paid, and the ledger is long.
Go quickly. I am weary of hearing your boasts, and my oath to tolerate you ends the moment you cross that hill.
Hold a moment more, ser {player}, and let me say it plainly: I shall remember this meeting every time I sharpen my sword. Good day.
Begone, and do not darken the next crossroads with your presence. The gods have tested me enough today, and you were the last trial.
When next we meet, ser {player}, I hope you bring better manners and a smaller company of fools. Until then, travel poorly.
Safe travels, ser {player}. Our paths have crossed without incident, which in these hills is as much as either of us can hope for.
We part as strangers, which suits me. Keep your business to yourself and I shall keep mine, and the road will remain peaceable.
The sun is low and my horse is tired. Farewell, ser {player}, and may the next traveller you meet be less tiresome than I was.
I have heard nothing to make me love you, nor anything to make me fear you. Go on your way, ser {player}, and I shall go on mine.
A pleasant enough exchange. I shall forget your face by supper, but I do not doubt you will be remembered in some other tavern.
Go well. There is a tollhouse two leagues east, and I would advise you pay the toll without argument, as I did.
Farewell, ser {player}. Weigh your words carefully in the next town; the magistrates there have longer memories than I do.
I wish you neither fortune nor misfortune. Walk the road as you please, and keep your hand away from my saddlebags.
We have said what needed saying. The wind is turning and so am I, ser {player}. Good day to you.
Ser {player}, the matter is closed for now. Should our paths cross again, we shall greet each other as cautiously as we did today.
Go with honour, ser {player}, and may your road be kind. I shall keep a seat by the hearth for you when you return.
Farewell, dear friend. Tell the wardens of the eastern keep that I sent you, and they will open their gates without a question.
My blade is yours should you need it, ser {player}. Ride on with my blessing and do not let the rain soften your resolve.
What a fine companion you have been on this road. I shall raise a cup to your name tonight, and I mean every word of it.
Until we meet again, ser {player}. The ancestors of both our houses would be proud of the courage you showed on this hill.
Parting is a sorrow, though a small one. Go, ser {player}, and bring back a tale worthy of the minstrels who will sing it.
Keep your head high and your banner unfurled, ser {player}. The realm is better for having an honest traveller upon its roads.
Go in peace, friend. I have left a token of goodwill in your saddlebag; open it only when the road grows long and lonely.
I will not forget that you stood beside me when the wolves came out. Farewell, ser {player}, and fortune favour your steps.
Ride swiftly and return soon, ser {player}. My table is always set for those whose word is as good as their steel.
